name: Rich notification media attachments
plain: Attaches images, audio or video to an iOS alert: 10 MB, 5 MB and 50 MB limits.
meaning: Fetched media can reveal when and where an alert was shown through the request. Android notifications show images via BigPictureStyle with no published size cap.

android.persistence: Downloaded by the app; memory bound
android.note: No published size limit; large bitmaps bound by memory

ios.persistence: Attachment files are moved into the notification store; cleaned after dismissal
ios.note: Audio 5 MB (AIFF, WAV, MP3, M4A), image 10 MB (JPEG, GIF, PNG), movie 50 MB (MPEG, MPEG-2, MP4, AVI)

limits.headline: Can attach pictures, sound or video to an iPhone alert, within size limits
limits.user_action: You get a push with a photo, clip or audio attached
can: Show an image up to 10 MB, like JPEG, GIF or PNG
Attach audio up to 5 MB or a movie up to 50 MB
Show large images on Android, limited only by memory
cannot: Attach files bigger than 10 MB, 5 MB or 50 MB for image, audio or movie
Use file types outside the allowed list
Show media if notifications are off for the app
limits.differs: iPhone sets size limits by type. Android has no published size limit but depends on memory.

story.what_it_is: Alerts that carry a picture, sound or short video.

marketing.name: Notification attachments
marketing.pitch: Apple lets alerts include images, audio or video that appear when the alert is expanded.

marketing.name: Expandable notifications
marketing.pitch: Android lets alerts expand to show a large picture or longer text.

story.for_you: You see a photo in the alert, like your delivery driver or a news picture. You may not know the picture was loaded from a web address that tells the sender it was shown.
story.for_makers: Makers get richer, more clickable alerts. The picture link can also carry a hidden ID that shows when and from where the alert was opened.

use_cases.example: A food app shows a photo of your order with the alert.
A news app shows a big photo with the headline.
A social app shows the photo someone sent you.
A store shows a product picture in a price drop alert.
A music app shows album art and a short audio preview.
A marketing tool hides a tracking pixel in the image link to know the alert was seen.
A sports app shows a short highlight video clip with the score alert.

story.android_note: Android shows big pictures with no published size cap.
story.ios_note: iOS limits attachments to 10 MB for images, 5 MB for audio and 50 MB for video.

technical_bounds: Fetching the media requires network work inside the extension window
